decisions.reason: The programming-port role does not change the already selected USB-C connector or its sourceability requirements.
The message confirms the existing USB-C and LDO standalone-operation arrangement without changing its regulator, activation condition, powered rail, or source-selection behavior.
Mentioning an LED connector on the main board does not change the LED supply, GPIO, level shifting, or power-control requirements.
The same source message already has a complete candidate MODIFY selecting the ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 module.
Identifying the USB-C connector as a programming port does not alter the separate 5V boost rail's enable control, loads, or output rating.
The same source message already introduces the relevant button, reset, touch, and BOOT-button elements for this candidate.
The message identifies the module and programming port but establishes no new GPIO assignment or compatibility rule.
USB-C is only a historical spatial reference in this candidate; the main-board programming-port role does not change power-board connector placement or accessibility.
The source concerns the main board and does not alter the power board's dimensions, orientation, mounting, or USB-C edge placement.
Confirming an INA219 on the 3.3V rail and excluding power management from the main board does not change the established DCDC1 voltage, rating, or normal-operation role.
The generic listing of pull-ups and series resistors as main-board passives does not change their existing values, topology, location, or population policy.
The source does not discuss charge-status signaling or alter the addressable-LED and dedicated charge-LED interface requirements.
